lens: Frontend-UX: WCAG 2.2 AA conformance, buildable user-story coverage, PRD UX-grade, ADR-0272 cookie consent non-dark-pattern compliance, cross-surface UX consistency.
wcag_2_2_aa_coverage_rationale: UX standard §3 enumerates every WCAG 2.2 AA SC explicitly (1.4.3 contrast 4.5:1, 1.4.11 non-text 3:1, 2.4.11 Focus Not Obscured Minimum, 2.5.7 Dragging Movements with keyboard alternative, 2.5.8 Target Size, 3.2.6 Consistent Help, 3.3.7 Redundant Entry, 3.3.8 Accessible Authentication Minimum). AAA-equivalents (2.4.12, 2.4.13, 3.3.9) reserved for regulated packs. CI gate oya-check-a11y-discipline backed by axe-core + pa11y + native runners. Pre-vetted contrast pairs in design tokens (§2.1.2) with 4.5:1+ on every fg/bg pair. Each of the three product PRDs (Messenger FR-42 + AC-35, Mail §7.1, Community FR-44 + AC-19 + §12.9) cites WCAG 2.2 AA as Must with CI-lane verification. ADR-0272 D-9 enumerates twelve concrete WCAG SCs for the CMP modal specifically and gates them via lean-pr-cmp-wcag-2-2-aa. Concrete gap: AAA promotion criteria for regulated packs is mentioned but no per-pack mapping ('healthcare → AAA' is asserted but the compliance pack registry does not explicitly bind AAA to pack-us-healthcare or pack-kr-medical).
ux_consistency_across_surfaces_rationale: Cross-surface tokens (design tokens §2.1–2.7) are single-source: identical Tailwind / SwiftUI / Compose / GTK / WinUI / Leptos mappings (§2.8). Strings via Fluent source-of-truth (§5) with 17+ day-one locales matched across Messenger FR-43 (17), Community 18-locale baseline, Mail JMAP-locale-passthrough. Keyboard shortcuts (§8.2) are explicitly aligned with industry leaders (Gmail-style for Mail j/k/e/r/c, Slack-style for Messenger Cmd+K/J, Google-Calendar-style for Calendar). Per-product UX baselines (§18) restate the per-product latency + UX rules consistently. Three consistency gaps observed: (a) B2C user-stories cite 18 locales; Messenger PRD FR-43 cites 17 locales — a one-locale drift (B2C adds tr-TR not in messenger list); (b) Density tiers (§7) define three tiers, but Messenger / Mail / Community PRDs do not cite which tier they default to; (c) The shared cross-product mention surface (`@user`, `#channel`, `&role`) is asserted in Community FR-30 + Messenger FR-06 but the resolution-via-Ontology contract is only fully specified in Messenger; Community + Mail rely on the Ontology mention substrate without restating the latency budget.

dark_pattern_risks.evidence: ADR-0272 D-3 explicitly forbids a default 'Accept all' button but RESERVES tenant-enable capability: 'An Accept all button MAY be tenant-enabled per D-11 ONLY if the tenant has signed acknowledgement that they accept the legal risk and ONLY if the tenant's jurisdiction profile does not forbid it. The default tenant policy is to not enable it.'
dark_pattern_risks.rationale: The seam is gated (legal-risk acknowledgement + jurisdiction check + default-off + dark-pattern-lint via oya gate validate dark-pattern-lint). EDPB Dark Patterns Guidelines 03/2022 prohibit 'Accept all' as DEFAULT presentation; ADR-0272 never ships it as default. The tenant-enable path is comparable to other GDPR-aligned multi-tenant CMP architectures (Iubenda enterprise tier). Risk is LOW because (1) the default is forbidden, (2) jurisdiction overlay D-7 strictest-wins forbids enabling it in EU/KR/KSA/BR; (3) lean-pr-cmp-dark-pattern-lint runs at build time. Mitigation already specified.
dark_pattern_risks.recommendation: Add explicit Cedar policy fragment that REFUSES Accept-all enablement when applied jurisdiction overlay set intersects {EU-GDPR, EU-ePrivacy, KR-PIPA, KSA-PDPL, BR-LGPD, UK-GDPR, CH-revFADP}. Track as IP-level concern in ADR-0272 implementation surface (already partially covered by D-7 + D-11 + Cedar pack/eu-gdpr/cedar/consent.cedar; add an explicit deny-rule rather than relying on default-off).

dark_pattern_risks.evidence: UX standard §10.7 + B2C cross-cutting principle 'Optimistic UI' specify optimistic mutations everywhere except money-moving/audit-relevant actions. Messenger §18.1 reiterates 'Optimistic send with rollback on failure.' Mail §7.1 'Aggressive prefetch'. The dark-pattern risk is silent rollback: if a sent-message visually 'sent' but server rejected, user may not notice the rollback toast (especially if toast auto-dismiss in 3s per §12.5 'Confirmation' default).
dark_pattern_risks.rationale: UX standard §10.7 explicitly mandates 'On failure: rollback + toast with Couldn't send. Retry?'. Severity is LOW because rollback is mandated, but the 3s auto-dismiss is borderline; failed-action toasts should persist longer.
dark_pattern_risks.recommendation: Amend UX standard §12.5: failed-action toasts (error severity from rollback) should use 10s auto-dismiss minimum AND persist in the in-app activity feed. Already partially specified ('Error: toast 10s + in-app + persist in feed'); cross-link from §10.7 to §12.4 severity table to remove ambiguity for engineers reading §10.7 alone.

dark_pattern_risks.evidence: Messenger PRD §7.1.3 says 'KakaoTalk-grade sticker UX: sticker tray with categories, recents, favourites; tap-to-send; hold-to-preview.' Sticker monetization is a known dark-pattern surface (Kakao tray pushes paid stickers above free recents in Korea).
dark_pattern_risks.rationale: Messenger PRD does not mention paid-sticker monetization or marketplace upsell in the sticker tray. The pattern is functional, not commercial. Tap-to-send + hold-to-preview is a standard CJK regional pattern, not coercive.
dark_pattern_risks.recommendation: If a future sticker marketplace surface emerges (cited as roadmap in messenger PRD §7.1.4), it must be added as a separate facet review (F10-r2) before launch.

dark_pattern_risks.risk: Mail 'auto-archive after send-receive-return' avoidance lacks explicit anti-pattern Cedar gate
dark_pattern_risks.evidence: Mail PRD §7.2 lists 'Auto-archive after send-receive-return' as an avoid anti-pattern. The avoidance is policy-only; no CI lane or Cedar gate enforces it.
dark_pattern_risks.rationale: Avoidance is documented and the default behavior (archive only on explicit E) is implemented per §7.2. Risk is informational only because no behavior-test gate exists to prevent regression.
dark_pattern_risks.recommendation: Add a behavior-test acceptance row to Mail PRD AC: 'reply-to-thread does NOT auto-archive (verified by integration test).' Track as Mail PRD IP enhancement.

dark_pattern_risks.evidence: Community PRD §9.2 lists 'AMA spam' (ask-mode windows enforced) and 'Slack-style ephemerality where users expect persistence' as avoid patterns. Both are policy-enforced via Cedar fragments (FR-13 automod + FR-29 slowmode).
dark_pattern_risks.rationale: Both patterns are explicitly enumerated and gated by tenant policy + Cedar.

dark_pattern_risks.risk: Cookie banner modal dismiss path on first visit
dark_pattern_risks.evidence: ADR-0272 D-3 modal layout shows three buttons: 'Save my choices', 'Reject non-essential', 'Accept selected'. Per Alt-8 (rejected), oyatie uses modal-overlay not full-page-interstitial. But the ADR is silent on whether closing the modal via X without choosing equals 'Reject non-essential' (default-deny) OR re-presents the modal.
dark_pattern_risks.rationale: Per GDPR Article 4(11) consent must be 'clear affirmative action'. If X closes the modal without persisting any consent state, the page must treat the visitor as having declined non-essential (default-deny). If the page re-presents the modal on next interaction, this risks a 'persistence-until-accept' pattern which CNIL 2024 flags as coercive even though not technically a dark pattern.
dark_pattern_risks.recommendation: Amend ADR-0272 D-3 to specify: 'Closing the modal via X without explicit choice is equivalent to Reject non-essential and writes a consent record with all non-necessary purposes = false. The CMP MUST NOT re-present the modal within the consent validity window unless taxonomy expansion occurs (D-1).' This makes the X-button safe-default explicit and reinforces ADR-0272 D-9 'No re-prompting within the consent validity period.'

dark_pattern_risks.evidence: UX standard §22.1 says 'AI features are off by default for new tenants and new users'. ADR-0272 forbids pre-checked opt-ins for cookies. The AI-disclosure card (§22.2) shows '[ Disable AI in this view ]' implying AI is already running when card surfaces.
dark_pattern_risks.rationale: The card is shown on 'first use' (after user explicitly enabled AI), not pre-emptively. Per ADR-0219 'no-code-first UX with optional AI assist', the assist-is-opt-in invariant holds. The card placement is correct, but the wording could be misread.
dark_pattern_risks.recommendation: Amend UX standard §22.2 to clarify card timing: 'First time AI is invoked by a user-initiated action (e.g., user clicks Generate-draft), the disclosure card appears BEFORE the AI runs, and AI execution proceeds only on the user clicking Continue.' This eliminates ambiguity about whether AI ran before disclosure.

buildability_assessment.rationale: B2B work-surfaces user stories explicitly declare intern_buildable_bar: true. Both compendiums use the 'Story ID / Persona / Context / Precondition / Step-by-step actions / Expected behaviors / Edge cases / Error cases / Success outcome / Failure recovery' structure that an entry-level engineer can transcribe into screen + API calls + acceptance test. The structure passes the 'one persona / one outcome / one surface / fits in ten lines' constraint. Persona rosters are closed (5 B2C + 12 B2B). Cross-reference: every story names the owning µservice entry-point per ADR-0245.
buildability_gaps: B2B user-stories file is 3,317 lines; without a story-ID prefix table at the top, navigating to a specific story requires text search. Add a story-ID index near §2.
B2C user-stories file has 5 personas vs B2B's 12 — the asymmetry is intentional (consumer fewer roles) but the rationale is not stated. Add a one-line note in B2C §2.

Neither user-stories file restates the WCAG 2.2 AA acceptance criterion per story; relies on the cross-cutting principle 'Accessibility by default' in B2C §1.3 and the global UX standard. Acceptable, but adds reviewer load.

messenger_prd.ux_section_lines: Section 7 (UX Strive/Avoid) covers 14 strives + 12 avoids. §3.11 Themes/A11y/i18n table cites WCAG 2.2 AA + screen-reader + RTL + 17 locales. FR-41 through FR-43 explicitly cover dark-mode + accessibility + i18n as Must.
messenger_prd.rationale: Cites industry leaders (Signal/Telegram/KakaoTalk/Line/WhatsApp/Instagram-DM/Discord/iMessage/Slack/Matrix). UX rules are specific (typing indicator dampened 500ms; read-receipt symmetric a la Signal). Latency budgets (§10.1) are p50/p99/p999 with concrete numbers.

mail_prd.ux_section_lines: Section 7 (UX strive-for/avoid) covers 11 strives + 17 avoids. §10.1 latency table includes compose-open, send, fetch, search, smart-compose, smart-reply, compose-to-workflow-handoff latency targets.
mail_prd.rationale: Keyboard-first (Superhuman parity) + 100ms target + JMAP cache + tracker-pixel-blocking + per-account context switching <50ms. The avoid-list is rigorous: tracker-pixel-default, auto-mark-as-read, auto-archive, ad-insertion, persistent identity disclosure, AI-hallucination-as-truth all explicitly forbidden.

community_prd.ux_section_lines: Section 9 (UX Strive/Avoid) covers 7 strives + 8 avoids. §12.9 Accessibility cites WCAG 2.2 AA + keyboard nav + screen-reader-compatible. FR-44 user-story for accessibility.
community_prd.rationale: Reference patterns named (Discord, Stack Overflow, Notion, Discourse, GitHub Discussions, Zendesk, ActivityPub). Voting hygiene (Wilson-confidence-interval ranking) is research-grade. Brigade detection + reputation-weighted voting are non-trivial UX-substrate decisions. KB-rot freshness signal is a maturity tell. AC-19 explicitly tests 'WCAG 2.2 AA verified via automated lighthouse + manual screen-reader audit. Keyboard-only navigation for all actions.'

findings.title: ADR-0272 D-3 cookie modal X-button dismiss behavior undefined
findings.evidence: ADR-0272 D-3 enumerates three explicit buttons (Save my choices / Reject non-essential / Accept selected) and shows an X close affordance in the layout sketch. However, the ADR is silent on the semantic of dismissing the modal via X without explicit choice. Per CNIL 2024 guidance, ambiguity here is a coercion risk; per GDPR Art 4(11), consent requires 'clear affirmative action' which the X close does not provide.
artifact_refs: docs/decisions/ADR-0272-cookie-consent-per-purpose-analytics-opt-in.md §D-9 'No re-prompting within the consent validity period'
findings.remediation: Amend D-3: 'Closing the modal via X without explicit button click MUST be equivalent to Reject non-essential (default-deny). The CMP writes a consent record with necessary=true and all other purposes=false. The modal MUST NOT re-present within the validity window unless taxonomy expands.' Add this clause to /specs/cookie-consent-schema.json as ui.interaction_kind enum value 'modal-dismissed-as-deny'.

findings.title: ADR-0272 D-11 tenant Accept-all enable seam lacks explicit Cedar deny for EU/KR/KSA/BR jurisdictions
findings.evidence: ADR-0272 D-11 says 'Enable Accept all surfaces only if their jurisdiction profile permits it and they sign acknowledgement (D-3).' Default-off + jurisdiction overlay is the protection, but no explicit Cedar deny-rule is named. Without a deny-rule, a misconfigured tenant could surface Accept-all in an EU subsidiary surface.
artifact_refs: docs/decisions/ADR-0272-cookie-consent-per-purpose-analytics-opt-in.md §D-3 'oyatie does not ship that pattern at all'
findings.remediation: Add explicit forbid rule to pack/eu-gdpr/cedar/consent.cedar (and eu-eprivacy, kr-pipa, ksa-pdpl, br-lgpd, uk-gdpr, ch-revfadp) of the form: forbid (principal, action == Action::EnableAcceptAllButton, resource) when { resource.applied_jurisdiction_overlay.contains('EU-GDPR') }; Add CI lane lean-pr-cmp-accept-all-jurisdiction-forbid that property-tests the cross-product of (jurisdiction × tenant-accept-all-enabled) and asserts the deny.

findings.title: Locale count drifts between B2C (18 locales) and Messenger PRD FR-43 (17 locales)
findings.evidence: B2C user-stories §1.3 'Localization day-one' enumerates 18 locales: ko, ja, zh-Hans, zh-Hant, en-US, en-GB, es-ES, es-LATAM, pt-BR, pt-PT, de, fr, it, nl, ru, ar, he, hi, id, vi, tr. Messenger PRD FR-43 says '17 languages day-one' and lists 17 in §7.1.14 (en, ko, ja, zh-Hans, zh-Hant, es, pt, fr, de, it, nl, ru, ar, hi, id, vi, th). Differences: B2C splits en-US/en-GB and es-ES/es-LATAM and pt-BR/pt-PT (regional variants) and adds tr+he but lacks th. Messenger collapses variants and includes th.
artifact_refs: docs/standards/ux-best-practices.md §5.2 'Tier-1 Western + Tier-1 CJK+APAC + Tier-1 RTL'
findings.remediation: Reconcile to a single canonical locale list in UX standard §5.2 (which currently enumerates ~20 locales across Tier-1 buckets). All PRDs + user-stories should cite a single normative source-of-truth. Recommend adding /specs/canonical-locale-set.json as authoritative pinned list; downstream PRDs cite it rather than restating.

findings.title: Three density tiers defined but no per-product default declared
findings.evidence: UX standard §7 defines spacious/comfortable/compact. §7 says 'Comfortable (default)' platform-wide but §4.3 says 'Denser content (use compact density tier by default for power users in the tenant admin console).' Messenger / Mail / Community PRDs do not state their default density.
findings.remediation: Amend UX standard §18 (Per-Product UX Baselines) to add a density-default row per product. Recommended defaults: Messenger=comfortable, Mail=compact (power-user surface, mirrors Superhuman density), Community=comfortable, Calendar=comfortable, Drive=comfortable, Docs=comfortable, Workflow-Studio=compact, Tenant-Admin=compact.

findings.title: AAA promotion criteria for regulated packs cited but not bound to specific packs
findings.evidence: UX standard §3 says 'WCAG 2.2 AA is the minimum for every shipped surface. AAA for regulated packs (healthcare, EU AI Act high-risk, government).' But no explicit mapping in pack/us-healthcare/, pack/kr-medical/, pack/eu-ai-act-annex-iii/ ties AAA conformance to the pack's certification levels (ADR-0251).
findings.remediation: Amend ADR-0207 + ADR-0251: declare which compliance packs REQUIRE WCAG 2.2 AAA. Suggested binding: pack/us-healthcare (HIPAA ·1557 a11y), pack/eu-ai-act-annex-iii (EU AI Act Art 9 risk management), pack/government-section-508 (US federal), pack/kr-medical-ema (KR PIPA + medical-device). Add CI lane oya-check-a11y-aaa-discipline that runs axe-core AAA ruleset against any surface that imports an AAA-required pack.

findings.title: Optimistic-UI rollback toast duration ambiguous between §10.7 and §12.5
findings.evidence: UX standard §10.7 says 'On failure: rollback + toast with Couldn't send. Retry?' but does not specify duration. §12.5 confirmation toast default = 3s; error toast default = 10s. Engineers reading §10.7 alone may use 3s.
findings.remediation: Amend §10.7 to add: 'Rollback toasts are Error severity per §12.4. Auto-dismiss = 10s, persist in in-app feed, action button (Retry) extends to sticky.' Add cross-link from §10.7 to §12.4 + §12.5.

findings.title: B2B user-stories (3,317 lines) and B2C user-stories (2,314 lines) lack story-ID indices
findings.evidence: Both compendiums are intern-readable but lack a top-of-file story-ID table. Finding a specific story requires text-search.
findings.remediation: Add a story-ID index near §2 of each compendium, listing every story ID + persona + one-line summary + line-anchor. Generator script lives at tools/user-stories/build-index.sh and runs in CI.

cross_facet_signals_for_synthesis: F7 (security): ADR-0272 D-12 audit-chain coverage + signed consent records aligns with security facet expectations.
F9 (compliance): ADR-0272 amends ADR-0099 + ADR-0251; per-jurisdiction overlay D-7 strictest-wins is the compliance authoring contract.
F11 (observability): ADR-0272 implementation surface adds substrate event bus emissions + audit-chain rows; per-tenant CMP usage telemetry is implicit.
F4 (ergonomic): UX standard §8 keyboard shortcut surface + Cmd+K palette align with ergonomic facet.
A1 (naming): five-purpose closed enum (necessary/preference/statistics/marketing/personalization) follows ADR-0099 + ADR-0105 closed-enum doctrine.
A3 (structure): every product PRD has consistent §-numbering for UX (§7 in Messenger+Mail, §9 in Community) — minor structural drift but functionally consistent.
verdict_rationale: The keystone bundle's frontend-UX surface is unusually strong: the UX best-practices standard is 2,489 lines of operational, CI-enforceable detail; WCAG 2.2 AA is enumerated SC-by-SC across the standard and the three product PRDs; ADR-0272 explicitly forbids the standard cookie-consent dark patterns (pre-checked, prominence-asymmetry, Accept-all-default, geofenced presentation, bundled consent); user-story compendiums (5,631 combined lines across B2C+B2B) meet the intern-buildable bar; cross-stack design tokens + Fluent i18n source + closed-enum locale set + per-product keyboard-shortcut tables show single-source-of-truth discipline. CONDITIONAL_PASS rather than PASS because of seven findings (2 MEDIUM, 4 LOW, 1 INFORMATIONAL) plus seven dark-pattern risks (all LOW or INFORMATIONAL after mitigations). The two MEDIUM items — F10-01 (modal X-dismiss semantic) and F10-02 (Cedar deny-rule for tenant Accept-all in regulated jurisdictions) — should be resolved before keystone merge because both are interpretive surfaces a regulator could probe. The remaining items are documentation-quality drifts (locale-count, density-default, AAA-pack-binding, toast-duration cross-section drift, story-ID index) that should land in follow-up IPs but do not block keystone-bundle admission. The dark-pattern audit lint (lean-pr-cmp-dark-pattern-lint) catches most regression vectors automatically, which is the right authoritative gate.
blockers_for_keystone_merge: F10-01 (ADR-0272 D-3 modal X-dismiss semantic clarified to default-deny + no-re-prompt)
F10-02 (Cedar forbid rule on Accept-all enablement in EU/KR/KSA/BR/UK/CH packs)
follow_up_ips: F10-04 per-product density-default table in UX standard §18
F10-05 AAA-required compliance pack binding (ADR-0207 + ADR-0251 amendment)
top_findings_summary: MEDIUM: ADR-0272 cookie modal X-button dismiss semantic undefined — must default-deny + no-re-prompt.
MEDIUM: tenant Accept-all enable seam lacks explicit Cedar deny in EU/KR/KSA/BR/UK/CH packs.
LOW: locale count drift between B2C user-stories (18) and Messenger PRD (17); reconcile via canonical-locale-set spec.
LOW: density-tier defaults not declared per product; add to UX standard §18.
LOW: WCAG 2.2 AAA promotion criteria cited but not bound to specific compliance packs.
LOW: optimistic-UI rollback toast duration cross-section drift (§10.7 vs §12.5).
INFO: user-stories compendiums lack story-ID indices.
